extracted_concepts.name: Sample Space
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Set of all possible outcomes of a random experiment.

extracted_concepts.name: Event
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: A subset of the sample space representing a specific outcome condition.

extracted_concepts.name: Axioms of Probability
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Foundational rules: non-negativity, normalization to 1, and countable additivity.

extracted_concepts.name: Conditional Probability
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Probability of an event occurring given that another event has already occurred.

extracted_concepts.name: Bayes' Theorem
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Rule for updating prior probabilities based on new evidence or likelihoods.

extracted_concepts.name: Independence
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Property where joint probability equals the product of marginal probabilities.

extracted_concepts.name: Random Variable
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Function mapping outcomes from sample space to real numbers.

extracted_concepts.name: Probability Mass Function
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Function specifying probability that a discrete random variable equals a specific value.

extracted_concepts.name: Binomial Distribution
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Distribution counting successes in a fixed number of independent Bernoulli trials.

extracted_concepts.name: Poisson Distribution
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Distribution modeling the number of events occurring in a fixed interval.

extracted_concepts.name: Probability Density Function
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Function describing relative likelihood for a continuous random variable.

extracted_concepts.name: Cumulative Distribution Function
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Function giving probability that variable takes value less than or equal to x.

extracted_concepts.name: Normal Distribution
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Symmetric bell-shaped distribution characterized by mean and variance.

extracted_concepts.name: Expectation
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Weighted average of all possible values of a random variable.

extracted_concepts.name: Variance
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Measure of dispersion around the mean, defined as expected squared deviation.

extracted_concepts.name: Covariance
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Measure indicating how two random variables vary together.

extracted_concepts.name: Correlation Coefficient
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Normalized covariance measuring strength and direction of linear relationship.

extracted_concepts.name: Law of Large Numbers
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Theorem stating sample mean converges to expected value as sample size grows.

extracted_concepts.name: Central Limit Theorem
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Theorem stating standardized sum of independent variables approaches normal distribution.

extracted_concepts.name: Sample Mean
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Arithmetic average of observed values in a statistical sample.

extracted_concepts.name: Sample Variance
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Unbiased estimator of population variance calculated from sample deviations.

extracted_concepts.name: Chi-squared Distribution
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Distribution of sum of squares of k independent standard normal variables.

extracted_concepts.name: Student's t-distribution
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Distribution used for inference when sample size is small and population variance unknown.

extracted_concepts.name: F-distribution
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Distribution of ratio of two scaled chi-squared variables.

extracted_concepts.name: Maximum Likelihood Estimation
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Parameter estimation method maximizing the likelihood function given observed data.

extracted_concepts.name: Unbiasedness
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Property where the expected value of an estimator equals the true parameter.

extracted_concepts.name: Confidence Interval
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Range of plausible values for a population parameter at a specified confidence level.

extracted_concepts.name: Null Hypothesis
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Baseline assumption in testing that no effect or difference exists.

extracted_concepts.name: Z-test
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Parametric test for population mean when population variance is known.

extracted_concepts.name: t-test
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Parametric test for population mean when population variance is estimated from sample.

extracted_relations.evidence: Formula explicitly computes posterior using P(B|A) and prior terms
Defined via P(AB) = P(A)P(B) which simplifies conditional probability
PMF assigns probabilities to discrete outcomes of X
PDF describes continuous distribution of X
F(x) is defined as integral of f(t)dt from -∞ to x
Computed as E(X²) - [E(X)]²
Calculated using E(XY) - E(X)E(Y)
ρ normalized by dividing Cov(X,Y) by product of standard deviations
States X̄ converges almost surely to population mean μ
Standardized sums converge in distribution to N(0,1)
For normal populations, sampling distribution of X̄ is N(μ,σ²/n)
Scaled sample variance (n-1)S²/σ² follows χ²(n-1)
Likelihood function L(θ) constructed as product of f(xᵢ;θ)
Definition requires E(θ̂) to equal true parameter θ
Interval bounds centered on X̄ ± critical value × standard error
Test statistic Z follows standard normal distribution under H₀
Test statistic T follows t-distribution with n-1 degrees of freedom
F statistic formed by ratio S₁²/S₂² of independent sample variances
Testing framework establishes H₀ before computing Z statistic
De Moivre-Laplace theorem approximates Binomial with Normal for large n
